sections.content: A gerund at the start of a sentence explains the method behind a historical achievement — how something was figured out, run, or built — without needing a separate clause. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Descifrando estos nudos poco a poco, los investigadores han demostrado que los quipus codificaban números.
items.english: By deciphering these knots little by little, researchers have shown that quipus encoded numbers.

items.spanish: Corriendo en relevos de pocos kilómetros cada uno, los chasquis podían llevar un mensaje entre Cusco y Quito en apenas unos días.
items.english: By running relays of just a few kilometres each, the chasquis could carry a message between Cusco and Quito in just a few days.

items.spanish: Experimentando con la agricultura en altura, los incas construyeron terrazas escalonadas en las laderas de las montañas.
items.english: By experimenting with high-altitude agriculture, the Inca built stepped terraces on mountain slopes.

items.spanish: Reuniendo quipus, caminos y terrazas, los incas construyeron un imperio inmenso sin necesitar nunca un sistema de escritura como el maya.
items.english: By combining quipus, roads and terraces, the Inca built an immense empire without ever needing a writing system like the Maya's.

sections.content: This opening-gerund pattern (*Descifrando..., Corriendo..., Experimentando..., Reuniendo...*) is one of the most common ways Spanish historical writing packs a method or cause into the front of a sentence — it usually answers "how did this happen?" before the main clause tells you what happened.
